messages:
Priya (Support): Hi team — opening thread for a customer escalation. Acme Health (private deployment) started seeing mTLS failures to our Private control plane after an egress firewall policy change yesterday. Symptoms: control plane connections drop during handshake, their LB/agent logs show repeated 'tls: handshake failure'.

Alex (Customer): Confirming. After the FortiGate update (7.4.2) we see failed calls from our control plane agent: we get ECONNRESET and agent logs show: 
```
2026-03-15T09:02:11Z agent main: rpc to controlplane.redwood.private:443 failed: tls: handshake failure
```
We captured a short pcap during repro and attached to the support ticket (s3://acme-support-pcaps/3162023456.pcap). The interesting bit in tcpdump: ClientHello shows TLSv1.3 but the supported_groups extension no longer contains x25519.

Alex (Customer): tcpdump excerpt: 
```
07:02:11.123456 IP 10.1.2.3.52345 > 54.23.198.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0,nop,wscale 7], length 0
07:02:11.124567 TLS ClientHello (len=512) TLSv1.3
  cipher_suites [AES128-GCM-SHA256, CHACHA20-POLY1305, AES256-GCM]
  supported_groups: secp256r1,secp384r1
  signature_algorithms: rsa_pss_rsae_sha256,rsa_pkcs1_sha256
```

Priya (Support): Noted — they lost x25519 and CHACHA ordering changed. Alex, can you confirm whether FortiGate's SSL Inspection profile is active for outbound to our host? Any DPI/TLS transform enabled?

Alex (Customer): Yes, they pushed a strict ssl-inspect profile that rewrites client TLS extensions to enforce FIPS-like curve lists for compliance. When we temporarily bypassed inspection for controlplane.redwood.private the agent handshake succeeded immediately.

Jordan (Eng-SRE): Thanks for the repro. That explains why handshake fails against our ECDSA-first cert profile (we prefer x25519/ECDHE). If the egress proxy removes x25519 and forces RSA-only curves, the client+server curve overlap can be empty and TLS1.3 handshake aborts. Can you share the pcap link + agent debug logs (with -v) so I can confirm the ServerHello rejection?

Alex (Customer): pcap and logs uploaded to the ticket: s3://acme-support-pcaps/3162023456.pcap and s3://acme-support-logs/3162023456-agent.log. We also verified that when we add an egress rule to exempt controlplane.redwood.private from SSL inspection (pass-through / no-decrypt), everything works.

Maya (Eng-ML): Quick triage note: our control plane currently presents ECDSA certs and prefers X25519 + secp256r1. We could add an RSA cert chain as a fallback for customers that must inspect TLS, but that has key management and security tradeoffs.

Jordan (Eng-SRE): Short-term remediation for customer: ask them to exempt our FQDN from TLS inspection OR allow x25519 and chacha20 on the inspection profile. Also ensure outbound allowlist includes our control plane IPs and that the inspector doesn't terminate the TLS session. Long-term options: product discussion on offering an RSA fallback or explicit guidance for Private deployments to avoid TLS-inspection for mTLS flows.

Priya (Support): Action items:
- Alex to disable SSL-inspect for controlplane.redwood.private and confirm (ASAP).
- Alex to share pcap + agent logs (done).
- Jordan/Maya to evaluate feasibility and risks of adding an RSA cert fallback; estimate ETA next week.

Alex (Customer): Will disable the inspect rule for the hostname now and post back. If that works we'll roll a config change to exempt Redwood endpoints permanently. Thanks for the rapid triage.

Priya (Support): Great — please ping here when you've validated. Adding @Jordan and @Maya to the ticket so eng can track the follow-up. :thumbsup:

Alex (Customer): Update 20 mins later — we disabled SSL-inspect for our control plane FQDN and the agent reconnected cleanly. No more handshake failures. Rolling change to prod exempt list now.

Priya (Support): Closing the immediate customer impact. We'll keep the ticket open for the product follow-up (RSA fallback discussion). Jordan, Maya — please add notes to the Private deployment checklist and Docs guidance about TLS inspection and recommend SNI/pass-through exemption for mTLS endpoints.

Jordan (Eng-SRE): Will do. I'll also add a short troubleshooting blurb to the KB: what to capture (pcap + agent verbose logs), how to check supported_groups in ClientHello, and the temporary workarounds.

support-bot: Ticket updated — escalation labeled 'controlplane-mtls-inspect-failure', priority P2, linked to ticket #SD-3294.
